item.title: Iran war enters its 6th week as military searches for downed jet crew member
item.summary: The war in Iran enters its 6th week as the search continues for the missing U.S. service member who bailed out of a fighter jet shot down over Iran on Friday.

item.title: 'London Falling': A teenage imposter, an aging gangster and a body in the Thames
item.summary: In 2019, 19-year-old Zac Brettler leapt towards the River Thames from a fifth-floor luxury apartment in central London. Patrick Radden Keefe investigates the story of the teen's double life in a new book.

item.title: Natural disasters and political instability hampered U.S. museum attendance in 2025
item.summary: The Art Newspaper's latest annual study of "the world's 100 most visited art museums" also reveals signs of modest growth.

item.title: Judge halts Trump effort requiring colleges to show they don't consider race in admissions
item.summary: A federal judge on Saturday said the Trump Administration the demand to collect data from universities was rolled out in a "rushed and chaotic" manner.

item.title: Opinion: Humanity's hopes ascended with Artemis II
item.summary: NPR's Scott Simon reflects on the successful launch of NASA's Artemis II this week. The four astronauts aboard will travel around the moon.

item.title: The busiest place you've never seen
item.summary: Photographer Julia Gunther and writer-filmmaker Nick Schönfeld chronicle the rhythms of daily life on Tristan da Cunha, the world's most remote inhabited island.

item.title: Buttercream wool and jelly bean eyes: The art of the Easter lamb cake
item.summary: The cakes – usually baked in the shape of a lamb using a special pan – have a long history in Central Europe, from the German osterlamm, to the Polish baranek wielkanocny, to the Alsatian lammele.

item.title: Tax refunds are trending a bit higher this year. Here's how people are spending them
item.summary: Some people are splurging. Others are finding that their refunds are being swallowed up by the rising cost of gas.

item.title: After the Minnesota surge, ICE is moving to a quieter enforcement approach
item.summary: ICE seems to be changing from aggressive immigration enforcement on city streets to an apparent return to operations that rely heavily on local law enforcement. But even in Florida, where sheriffs are required to cooperate with ICE, some conservative sheriffs have concerns abo...

item.title: When legal sports betting surges, so do Americans' financial problems
item.summary: As online betting has grown in popularity, a new report from the New York Federal Reserve builds on the troubling link between legal sports wagering and financial health.
